Scatterplot from the 2026 Ipsos AI Monitor comparing excitement and nervousness about artificial intelligence across 32 countries. Each dot represents a country, positioned according to the percentage of respondents who say AI makes them excited and the percentage who say it makes them nervous. China and India are among the most enthusiastic, with 83% and 79% expressing excitement, respectively, while the United States (33%) and Canada (26%) are much less enthusiastic and more nervous. Broadly, countries in Asia and emerging economies tend to express greater excitement, while North American and European countries cluster toward the nervous, less excited end of the chart. Excitement and nervousness are measured separately, so respondents can express both feelings. The survey uses online samples, which disproportionately represent urban, educated, and affluent populations in some countries.

Source: https://www.ipsos.com/sites/default/files/ct/news/documents/2026-06/Ipsos-AI-Monitor-2026.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com

A dual-chart infographic displaying U.S. manufacturing employment data. The title reads: "Data-center supply industries added 57k jobs from Jan 2025 to Sep 2026 while the rest of manufacturing lost 68k".
The left chart is a line graph titled "Payroll employment, January 2019 = 100" covering the years 2015 to 2026. It plots five indices: All manufacturing (99.0), Manufacturing ex data-center industries (98.2), Durable goods manufacturing (98.5), Durable goods ex data-center industries (97.0), and a sharp upward-trending Data Centers Index (111.3) which accelerates after the release of ChatGPT in late 2022/early 2023.
The right chart is a bar graph titled "Change in payrolls, Jan 2025 to Sep 2026" showing job changes in thousands: Data-center exposed industries (+57k), All manufacturing (-11k), Manufacturing ex data-center industries (-68k), Durable goods manufacturing (+45k), and Durable goods ex data-center industries (-12k).
